你要阅读 NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra 技术报告并总结其后训练(post-training)方法学。PDF 地址: https://research.nvidia.com/labs/nemotron/files/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3-Ultra-Technical-Report.pdf 。当前日期 2026-08-02。

背景(我已从 NVIDIA-NeMo/RL 仓库的 ultra-v3 分支指南中得知):后训练 pipeline 为 SFT → Student RLVR(GRPO, 两阶段 49k→65k 上下文) → 多个专门化 teacher(General/Reasoning/RLHF/IFBench/SWE) → MOPD(Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation)。训练数据 blends 开源在 HF: nvidia/Nemotron-RL-Ultra-Training-Blends。模型是 550B-A55B 的 hybrid Mamba-Transformer MoE(LatentMoE + MTP),pretraining 用 NVFP4,上下文扩展到 1M。

步骤建议:
1. 用 `curl -L -o /tmp/nemotron_ultra.pdf "https://research.nvidia.com/labs/nemotron/files/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3-Ultra-Technical-Report.pdf"` 下载 PDF。
2. 检查环境是否有 `pdftotext`(poppler-utils);如果有,执行 `pdftotext -layout /tmp/nemotron_ultra.pdf /tmp/nemotron_ultra.txt`,然后分段 Read(用 Grep 定位关键词:post-training, SFT, RLVR, GRPO, MOPD, distillation, teacher, QAT, quantization, NVFP4, MTP, reward, GenRM, hyperparameter 等)。若无 pdftotext,用 `python3 -m venv /tmp/pdfenv2 && /tmp/pdfenv2/bin/pip install pypdf` 后写脚本提取。
3. 全文通读提取的文本(可分多次 Read),重点关注 post-training 章节。

请输出一份详细的中文结构化笔记,包含:
- 模型基本信息(架构、参数、上下文、pretraining 简要,包括 NVFP4 预训练做法)
- 后训练整体 pipeline 的完整阶段划分(报告中实际命名),各阶段顺序与目的
- SFT 细节:数据、配置
- RLVR 细节:GRPO 超参、reward/verifier 设计、环境/ Gym agent 类型(math, code, tool use...)、规模
- RLHF / GenRM 细节:judge 模型、pairwise 信号
- MOPD 细节:机制、teacher panel 构成、损失函数、on-policy 路由、几轮 iteration
- MTP Boosting / QAT / 量化相关后训练(如报告有)
- 数据与代码开源情况(报告里列的 HF 数据集和 GitHub 仓库)
- 关键 benchmark 结果(简要)
- 基础设施(GB200 集群规模、节点划分等,如有)

要求:所有数字务必从原文核实,不要臆造;找不到的信息明确说"报告未披露"。最后给出你提取的文本文件路径。

7	Abstract.
8	We introduce Nemotron 3 Ultra, a 550 billion total and 55 billion active parameter Mixture-of-Experts
9	Hybrid Mamba-Attention language model. We pre-trained Nemotron 3 Ultra on 20 trillion text
10	tokens, then extended the context length to 1M tokens, and post-trained using Supervised Fine Tuning
11	(SFT), Reinforcement Learning (RL), and Multi-teacher On-Policy Distillation (MOPD). Nemotron
12	3 Ultra is our most capable model yet, employing multiple key technologies - LatentMoE, Multi
13	Token Prediction (MTP), NVFP4 pre-training, multi-environment RLVR, MOPD, and reasoning
14	budget control. Nemotron 3 Ultra achieves up to∼ 6× higher inference throughput as compared
15	to state-of-the-art publicly available LLMs while attaining on-par accuracy. The state-of-the-art
16	accuracy, high inference throughput, and 1M token context length make Nemotron 3 Ultra ideal
17	for long-running autonomous agentic tasks. We open-source the base, post-trained, and quantized
18	checkpoints, along with the training data and recipe on HuggingFace.
19	1. Introduction
20	We present Nemotron 3 Ultra, the largest and most capable model in the Nemotron 3 family (Blake-
21	man et al., 2025). As LLM applications evolve from simple chatbots to long-running agents capable
22	of autonomously writing code, conducting research, and completing complex tasks, the ability to
23	deliver fast and efficient inference becomes increasingly important. Nemotron 3 Ultra addresses this
24	by employing a Mixture-of-Experts hybrid Mamba-Attention architecture, leading to improvements
25	along the inference-throughput-to-accuracy frontier. While Mixture-of-Experts help Nemotron 3
26	Ultra achieve better accuracy per active parameter, the hybrid Mamba-Attention architecture signifi-
27	cantly improves inference throughput by reducing attention cost and KV cache footprint. Nemotron 3
28	Ultra achieves 5.9×, 4.8×, and 1.6× higher inference throughput compared to GLM-5.1-754B-A40B,
29	Kimi-K2.6-1T-A32B, and Qwen-3.5-397B-17B respectively on 8K input / 64K output token setting
30	while also attaining on-par accuracy across a wide range of agentic and reasoning benchmarks.
31	We pretrained Nemotron 3 Ultra 550B-A55B Base with all the key Nemotron 3 features and
32	technologies (Blakeman et al., 2025), including NVFP4 pre-training, LatentMoE (Elango et al.,
33	2026), and Multi Token Prediction (MTP) (Gloeckle et al., 2024). We pretrained our base model in
34	NVFP4 with 20 trillion text tokens using a Warmup-Stable-Decay learning rate schedule. Pretraining
35	was divided into two phases with 15 trillion tokens of data in the first phase focusing on diversity
36	and broad domain coverage followed by 5 trillion tokens of data in the second phase focusing on high
37	quality data to refine model accuracy. LatentMoE helped us achieve better accuracy per parameter
38	than standard Granular MoEs (Dai et al., 2024) while Multi Token Prediction (MTP) leads to
39	faster inference with speculative decoding. Our pretrained base model achieves significantly higher
40	accuracy than other publicly available base models, such as DeepSeek v3.2 (DeepSeek-AI, 2025a),
41	Mistral Large 3, Kimi-K2 (Team, 2025), and GLM-4.5 (GLM-4.5-Team, 2025).

545	2.5. Long-Context Extension
546	Similar to Nemotron 3 Super & Nano, we added a long-context phase (LC-Phase) at the end of
547	pretraining. In the LC-Phase, we performed continuous pretraining (CPT) to equip the base model
548	with long-context ability. We used a constant learning rate of2.5* 10−6. We used 32-way context
549	parallelism, 8-way tensor parallelism, 128-way expert parallelism, and 2-way pipeline parallelism to
550	train on GB200 GPUs.
551	Besides the long-context document QA data we used in Nemotron 3 Super & Nano, we further added
552	long-context SFT-style data into the blend. We did not use any RULER-style data in the blend.
553	Overall, the long-context data was 46% and Phase 2 data was 54% in the blend. We performed
554	CPT on 1,048,576 (1M) context length for 92% of the iterations, while we trained on 4,096 (4K)
555	for the remaining 8% of the time in order to maintain the accuracy of the short benchmarks. Note
556	that each iteration was trained with either 1M or 4K length and we did not mix sequence lengths
557	within an iteration. Each iteration we constantly trained for 25,165,824 tokens. We only put math
558	and code SFT-style data into the 4K iterations, since we found it worked best to maintain the short
559	benchmark metrics while achieving strong long-context RULER scores. Eventually, the LC-Phase

847	3.1. Supervised Fine Tuning
848	To train the student model, we start from the pre-trained base model and perform Supervised
849	Fine-Tuning (SFT) in two stages, following Nemotron 3 Super (NVIDIA, 2026). In Stage 1, we train
850	on packed sequences of length294,912tokens with global batch size64for204 ,800samples, using a
851	cosine learning-rate schedule with peak learning rate1.5× 10−5, minimum learning rate1× 10−6,
852	and9 ,600warmup samples. In Stage 2, we extend packed sequence to515,000tokens, augmenting
853	the mixture with additional long-context data up to512K tokens. We train with global batch size64
854	for19 ,200samples, using the same learning-rate schedule with peak1× 10−5 to minimum2× 10−6
855	and6 ,400warmup samples. As in pre-training, we retain the shared-weight MTP objective during
856	SFT, using two MTP layers with a per-token auxiliary-loss scaling factor of0.1.
857	3.1.1. Data
858	Long Context.We prepare 512K long-context SFT data based on the synthetic data pipeline
859	following (NVIDIA, 2026). Our data is aimed at improving long-context abilities including, but not

864	Efficiency and Control.The SFT data include two components for reasoning efficiency and
865	control. The first is training samples generated by GPT-OSS-120B in its medium-effort mode on
866	prompts of math reasoning, STEM question answering and instruction following. These SFT data
867	initiate Ultra’s medium-effort mode which is later optimized during the RLVR stage. The second
868	component is training samples where the reasoning traces are truncated to random reasoning budgets
869	while the responses remain the same. This is similar to Nemotron 3 Nano and Super with one design
870	change: the</think>tokens in the truncated samples are masked from SFT training loss.

877	we translated the Nemotron 3 Super safety data blend into six languages — German, Spanish,
878	French, Japanese, Italian, and Chinese - using NeMo Skills’ chunked translation capability, ensuring
879	sentence-by-sentence parity, and paired with NVIDIA Riva Translate 4B v1.1 as the translation
880	backbone.

882	compared against the original English prompt-response pair. Examples with semantic similarity
883	below 0.8 were filtered out, removing approximately≈ 10− 15%of examples per translated language.
884	The highest- and lowest-scoring translations were manually spot-checked to verify that this filter
885	was removing examples with clear translation failures or structural issues. After filtering, we used
886	stratified sampling to create a balanced dataset across the six translated languages. The final safety
887	blend contains about≈ 135K samples:≈ 45K in English and≈ 15K from each of the translated
888	languages.

890	levels and tool-use harnesses to improve generalization.
891	First, we retain the search trajectories from the Nemotron 3 Super (NVIDIA, 2026) dataset,
892	whose seed prompts are grounded in the Wikidata knowledge graph. Specifically, the dataset
893	selects well-connected hub entities and performs 4–8 hop random walks over factual relations to
894	construct multi-hop search prompts. These prompts are then solved using Tavily Search Engine
895	(https://www.tavily.com/), with MiniMax 2.1 serving as the teacher model.
896	In addition, we include a new search dataset: a commercially cleared subset of OpenResearcher (Li
897	et al., 2026), a public SFT dataset designed for long-horizon research agents. OpenResearcher
898	synthesizes over97K trajectories using gpt-oss-120b (Agarwal et al., 2025) as the teacher model in

902	full document contents, andfind for locating exact textual evidence within an opened document.
903	The resulting trajectories capture long-horizon reasoning-action-observation loops in which the
904	model iteratively decomposes research questions, gathers and inspects sources, localizes supporting

906	OpenResearcher data; instead, we curated the commercial-OK portion by removing examples whose

1048	3.1.2. Data Packing
1049	To train efficiently on a large and diverse collection of datasets, we adopt a length-aware best-fit
1050	packing strategy (Ding et al., 2024), which packs multiple conversations into sequences up to a
1051	maximum context length. Our packer is highly memory-efficient: it reads and interleaves all source
1052	files in a round-robin fashion, maintains only a fixed-size pool of open sequences in memory, and
1053	retires a sequence once its residual capacity falls below a small tolerance. Each incoming conversation
1054	is assigned to the partially filled sequence whose remaining capacity it most tightly fits, following a
1055	best-fit rule that minimizes padding overhead. We neither truncate nor split conversations, preserving
1056	complete context and reducing hallucinations. Additionally, we enforce an in-pack deduplication
1057	19
1058	===== PAGE 20 =====
1059	Nemotron 3 Ultra : Open, Efficient Mixture-of-Experts Hybrid Mamba-Transformer Model for Agentic Reasoning
1060	constraint to prevent identical prompts from co-occurring within the same sequence. After packing,
1061	we perform a final shuffle over all completed packs. Overall, our implementation ensures that each
1062	packed sequence draws from a broad, well-mixed cross-section of the data distribution rather than
1063	clustering examples from any single source. This thorough mixing is essential at scale, where naive
1064	concatenation of per-source shards would otherwise induce strong distributional locality and degrade
1065	optimization stability.
1066	3.2. Reinforcement Learning
1067	To improve upon SFT model, we conduct a unified RLVR (Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable
1068	Reward) training stage spanning all available environments, targeting terminal usage, office and
1069	productivity workflows, software engineering, search, general tool-calling, math, code, STEM, safety,
1070	chat, instruction following, long-context QA, inductive and transductive reasoning, structured
1071	outputs, and general model usability. For harness-based environments, we construct training data
1072	using a diverse collection of harness implementations and interaction formats, improving robustness
1073	to variations in execution settings and reducing overfitting to any particular harness design.
1074	We refresh the RL training data using recent collections and perform reward profiling prior to training.
1075	For data mixture and curriculum construction, we adopt the Gaussian-based approach introduced
1076	in NVIDIA (2025b). Our training procedure largely follows the asynchronous GRPO algorithm with
1077	the stability optimizations proposed in NVIDIA (2026), while incorporating several improvements to
1078	the training infrastructure, detailed in Section 3.6. To support training across a large and diverse
1079	set of environments, we use a global batch size of 8192, with each sample generating 16 rollouts.
1080	Training begins with a maximum generation length of 48K tokens, which is later increased to 64K
1081	tokens.
1082	3.3. MOPD
1083	Mixed-environment RLVR provides broad capability improvements across a wide range of domains.
1084	However, as the number of environments continues to grow, each domain contributes only a relatively
1085	small number of samples to any given training batch, diluting the per-domain learning signal and
1086	making it increasingly difficult to balance training across domains. To fully unlock performance and
1087	push the frontier in each capability area, we train more than ten specialized teacher models, each
1088	optimized through its own domain-specific training pipeline.
1089	During MOPD, the student model (obtained from RLVR) generates rollouts across all domains
1090	and receives dense reward signals from the corresponding teacher models. To maximize efficiency,
1091	MOPD is conducted asynchronously, with student rollout generation, teacher scoring, and student
1092	optimization fully pipelined. Moreover, MOPD is performed over multiple iterative cycles: after
1093	obtaining an MOPD-trained checkpoint, we branch out new rounds of teacher training initialized from
1094	the updated student model and subsequently merge the resulting improvements back into the next
1095	MOPD stage. This iterative co-evolution between student and teachers enables continuous capability
1096	improvement and progressively stronger specialization across domains. On training Nemotron 3
1097	Ultra, we conduct two iterations of MOPD, with exact procedure shown in Figure 10.

1440	One key finding from our MOPD trials is that teacher models trained with substantially different
1441	training pipelines cannot be effectively combined through a straightforward MOPD merge, resulting in

1441	training pipelines cannot be effectively combined through a straightforward MOPD merge, resulting in
1442	suboptimal performance. We hypothesize that when the teacher and student are trained on different
1443	SFT data, they acquire different reasoning behaviors and induce different output distributions. This
1444	distribution mismatch can cause student-generated trajectories to be out-of-distribution for the
1445	teacher, reducing the quality and reliability of the supervision signals provided by the teacher. We
1446	encountered this issue in practice because the teacher and student models were developed in parallel,
1447	with many of the agentic and reasoning teachers trained using their own specialized SFT pipelines.

1449	warmup stage before MOPD. Specifically, the student undergoes a very light SFT on data drawn
1450	from the teacher’s training distribution. The objective is to align the student’s reasoning trajectories
1451	and output distribution with those expected by the teacher. This improves the reliability of teacher
1452	supervision by increasing the likelihood that student-generated trajectories remain within the
1453	teacher’s support. Since the warmup stage is intentionally limited in scale, it induces minimal
1454	regression on unrelated domains, and any residual degradation is subsequently recovered through
1455	MOPD training.

1512	3.3.5. Limitations and Open Problems
1513	In this section we will discuss several aspects of MOPD that remain unresolved and would benefit
1514	from further study. During the development of MOPD, we evaluated several technically plausible
1515	variants that did not improve performance under our current experimental setup. We share these
1516	observations to make the empirical picture more complete, but they should not be interpreted as
1517	evidence that these approaches are fundamentally ineffective. With further research, we believe
1518	these directions could yield MOPD approaches that outperform our current setup, and we encourage
1519	the community to continue exploring them.
1520	• Logit matching.A natural alternative to the sampled-token objective is distribution-level
1521	distillation, where the student is trained to match the teacher’s predictive distribution over
1522	the top-𝑘 tokens or the full vocabulary at each prefix. In our preliminary experiments, these
1523	objectives did not improve MOPD performance and consistently underperformed the sampled-
1524	token objective on some agentic benchmarks such as Terminal Bench. We hypothesize that
1525	full-distribution matching may impose an overly strong local constraint on prefixes sampled
1526	from the student policy, particularly when those prefixes have limited support under the teacher
1527	distribution. In this regime, teacher logits can become poorly calibrated or less informative,
1528	and matching the full distribution may amplify noise from off-support states. By contrast,
1529	the sampled-token objective applies supervision only to realized actions and may therefore

1533	provide a more stable on-policy learning signal. Characterizing when broader distributional
1534	supervision is beneficial remains an open problem.
1535	• Foundations for MOPD.As discussed above, MOPD is most effective when student-
1536	generated trajectories remain within the teacher’s support, allowing the teacher to provide
1537	reliable supervision. One possible approach is to ensure that the teacher and student share a
1538	unified SFT stage before specialization. Another is to first develop specialized teachers, use
1539	them to generate SFT data, and then train the student with this data before applying RL
1540	or MOPD. Due to time and resource constraints, we did not systematically evaluate these
1541	alternatives in this project and will leave them for future work.
1542	• MOPD on long-horizon tasks.Agentic workflows require many turns of tool calls and
1543	environment interactions, whereas reasoning tasks are typically single-turn. When mixing end-

1548	2026), for most of the agentic tasks. This approach performs relatively well, but whether
1549	end-to-end rollouts can yield further gains, and how to make it robust to potential distribution

1737	Ray GCS Scalability and Slurm Launch Overheads
1738	The NeMo-RL job is heterogeneous, it must launch different roles (training workers, vLLM generation
1739	workers, gym workers, and judge workers), each with different resource requirements, across different
1740	node subsets. At the start of post-training, our RL launch script issued multiple, separatesrun
1741	invocations per node to assign each node its role, start its processes, and monitor progress. Each
1742	srun is an RPC to the Slurm controller daemon (slurmctld), which must process them serially. At
1743	scale, this meant hundreds of serial RPCs queued againstslurmctld, a pattern that scaled𝑂(𝑛)
1744	with the node count and quickly became a scaling bottleneck. Restructuring to a single multi-node
1745	srun reduced Slurm controller interactions to𝑂(1). Together, startup cost dropped from over 30
1746	minutes to 10 minutes..
1747	Additionally, the RL job creates a massive number of Ray actors simultaneously across policy,
1748	generation, and environment workers. At 3K+ GPU scale, Ray’s single-threaded Global Control
1749	Service (GCS) was overwhelmed by actor registrations, causing long startups (25-49 minutes) and
1750	thundering-herd startup failures. We eliminated 40% of actor registrations by converting short-lived
1751	actors to tasks, pooling initialization actors per node, and applied aggressive GCS tuning. Anyscale
1752	resolved the GCS scalability regressions with the fixes shipped in the Ray 2.55 public release.
1753	Topology-Aware NVLink Domain Placement
1754	On GB200 NVL72, the NVLink domain spans an entire rack (72 GPUs across 18 nodes). Without
1755	topology awareness during worker placement, Megatron’s Expert Parallelism (EP) groups can span
1756	multiple racks, forcing MoE all-to-all communication over InfiniBand instead of NVLink.
1757	NeMo RL had no concept of NVLink domains: Ray node IDs are random UUIDs with no topological
1758	relation, and Megatron trusts the rank order it receives. If the framework assigns ranks without
1759	NVLink domain awareness, EP groups will silently span racks. The fix was to make rank assignment
1760	domain-aware and ensure all GPUs within an EP group are co-located on the same rack. Note that
1761	inter-rack ordering is not a concern here, as our DP size does not require exploiting cross-rack rail
1762	optimizations.
1763	The fix was threefold. First, at container startup (beforeray start ), ray.sub generates and sources
1764	a probe script that parses the NVLink fabricClusterUUID from nvidia-smi -q – a hex string
1765	identical for all GPUs in the same NVLink domain – and registers it as a Ray custom resource
1766	(nvlink_domain_<ClusterUUID>), giving the scheduler rack-membership information it previously
1767	lacked. The same probe derives a topology rank (topo_rank) from SLURM_TOPOLOGY_ADDR, falling
1768	back to SLURM_PROCID or hostname digits. Second, inside NeMo RL’sRayVirtualCluster, bundle
1769	indices are sorted by a( domain_min_topo_rank,topo_rank,gpu_id )composite key, ordering
1770	NVLink domains by their minimum topology rank and nodes within each domain by physical
1771	position, so that EP groups remain within a single NVLink domain. When segment_size is
1772	33

1775	set, bundles from domains that cannot contribute a complete segment are discarded. The sorted
1776	order drives per-worker RANK and CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES assignment, and Megatron runs with
1777	external_gpu_device_mapping=True so it trusts Ray’s GPU pinning rather than re-deriving device
1778	placement. Third, thetopo_rank (from SLURM_TOPOLOGY_ADDR) corrects the scrambled Slurm block
1779	ordering, with ray.sub additionally applying a deterministic hostname sort before Ray head-node
1780	assignment.
1781	With these changes, training and generation actors are co-located in the same NVLink domain, and
1782	EP all-to-all traffic stays on NVLink instead of falling back to InfiniBand.
1783	This optimization delivered a20% end-to-end throughput improvementon GB200.
1784	NUMA Binding for Policy and vLLM Workers
1785	On GB200 NVL72, each compute tray contains a Grace CPU with two sockets and multiple NUMA
1786	nodes. GPUs are physically affiliated with specific CPU sockets: GPUs 0 and 1 map to NUMA
1787	node 0, while GPUs 2 and 3 map to NUMA node 1. Without explicit NUMA binding, Ray worker
1788	processes, both Megatron policy workers and vLLM generation workers, could be scheduled on
1789	CPU cores belonging to the remote socket relative to their assigned GPUs. On Grace-Blackwell,
1790	the NVLink-C2C interconnect between Grace CPU and Blackwell GPU is socket-local, so cross-
1791	socket placement forces memory traffic to traverse the inter-socket coherence link before reaching
1792	NVLink-C2C, degrading GPU memory bandwidth.
1793	The fix was to explicitly bind policy and vLLM worker processes to the CPU socket local to their
1794	assigned GPUs. This ensures that optimizer state offloading (e.g., CPU↔GPU transfers during
1795	checkpointing and weight refit), tokenization, data preprocessing, and pinned-memory allocations all
1796	hit local DRAM and use the socket-local C2C path. This optimization delivered a10% end-to-end
1797	throughput improvementon GB200.

1799	Synchronous checkpoint saves blocked training for∼60s per save. Enabling asynchronous checkpoint-
1800	ing from the Nvidia Resiliency Extension (NVRx), where model parameters are copied to CPU and
1801	persisted in the background while training continues, reduced the exposed blocking time to∼6–8
1802	seconds. Two additional optimizations reduced this further: overlapped NCCL transfers with D2H
1803	copies to shrink the synchronous staging window, and persistent checkpoint worker processes that
1804	avoid fork/spawn overhead on each save. We further moved checkpoint finalization, the cross-worker
1805	synchronization and the final commit, onto a background thread so it never blocks training, and we
1806	cache the distributed save plan so it is computed once rather than on every save. With the Megatron
1807	Core Distributed Optimizer, which shards optimizer state across data-parallel ranks so each rank
1808	only saves its local slice, the exposed save time reduces to<1 second.

1842	Multi-node vLLM uses Ray as its distributed executor. Each vLLM data-parallel leader spawns

1844	At scale, this creates additional GCS connections on top of the actor creation burst. Beyond the JIT

1850	could not be reused by another, causing silent crashes at initialization.

1871	At scale, every node simultaneously reads the container image (∼44 GB squashfs) from shared
1872	storage at job startup, producing tens of terabytes of concurrent reads across thousands of parallel
1873	I/O streams. This overwhelmed the storage subsystem: a subset of nodes either hitInput/output
1874	error or stalled for 12+ minutes during container extraction (vs.∼2 to 3 minutes under normal
1875	conditions). Because all workers must be ready before Ray initialization begins, a single slow node
1876	delays the entire job. Additionally, at job completion all nodes concurrently write back JIT caches
1877	to shared storage, creating a second I/O storm that degraded storage availability for other jobs on
1878	the cluster.

1881	the container image, subsequent jobs reuse the cached local copy, effectively eliminating the
1882	shared storage read load for warm nodes.
1883	• Asymmetric read/write cache paths.During training, all JIT writes go to node-local
1884	storage, producing zero shared storage writes. At job completion, a single designated sidecar
1885	process archives the caches back to shared storage as compressed tarballs, rather than all nodes
1886	writing simultaneously. Since all nodes compile identical kernels, only one node’s cache needs
1887	to be persisted. At startup, each node extracts these tarballs into local storage via a single
1888	sequential read per cache type, avoiding metadata-intensive small-file I/O entirely.

2120	We selected the model’s bits-per-element (BPE) budget empirically, by quantizing a fixed intermediate
2121	checkpoint at a range of BPE settings and scoring each against a curated suite of evaluations, served

2123	to suppress run-to-run variance and report the averaged pass@1 scores. The suite spans seven
2124	benchmarks: coding (SciCode), scientific reasoning (GPQA Diamond, HLE, CritPt), instruction
2125	following and knowledge (IFBench, AA-Omniscience), and long-context reasoning (AA-LCR).
2126	The results are summarized in Table 13. Here BPE is best read as a summary axis over a family
2127	of quantization recipes rather than a single tunable knob: the higher-BPE points correspond to
2128	qualitatively different strategies (router-only quantization, keeping the last MoE layer in BF16, and
2129	skipping the top-8 most sensitive experts), each of which lands at a different effective BPE.

2257	4.5. SSM Cache Optimization
2258	In Mamba autoregressive decoding, the SSM state is stored in a constant-sized cache for each batch
2259	element. The KV cache size, on the other hand, grows with sequence length. However, there is a
2260	crossover point below which the Mamba cache size is larger than the KV cache size. For example, in
2261	Nemotron 3 Ultra, the 32-bit Mamba cache is larger than the FP8 KV cache at sequence lengths up
2262	to 64K. This is illustrated in Figure 14.
2263	Therefore, depending on the sequence length and batch size, the Mamba cache can become both a
2264	DRAM-footprint bottleneck and a source of DRAM-read pressure that limits decoding speed.
2265	To address this, we quantize the Mamba SSM cache from the original FP32 precision to lower
2266	precisions. Following Nemotron 3 Super (NVIDIA, 2026), we first adopt 16-bit cache precision,
2267	where FP16 with stochastic rounding preserves FP32-cache accuracy and verbosity.
2268	To further improve cache compression, we also explore 8-bit Mamba cache quantization formats. We
2269	evaluated this on Nemotron 3 Super.

2406	5. Inference
2407	Nemotron 3 Ultra inherits the inference-aware architecture of Nemotron 3 Super (NVIDIA, 2026):
2408	LatentMoE (Elango et al., 2026), which buys more routed experts at fixed inference cost by trading
2409	away hidden-dimension width; a hybrid Mamba-2 stack with sparse global Attention anchors,
2410	which gives sub-quadratic sequence-length scaling during prefill and a bounded KV-cache footprint
2411	during decode; and Multi-Token Prediction for native speculative decoding (see §2). Below we first
2412	characterize how these choices play out in practice across serving regimes — prefill- versus decode-
2413	heavy workloads and small- versus large-batch operation — and then turn to the considerations that
2414	come into focus when serving a model of this size, considerations that did not bind at Nemotron
2415	3 Super or Nemotron 3 Nano scale. Quantization recipes and the SSM-state cache treatment are
2416	covered in §4; headline throughput comparisons appear in §1.
2417	5.1. Performance across serving regimes
2418	Nemotron 3 Ultra’s effective inference performance depends strongly on the operating point: the
2419	prefill/decode balance of the workload and the batch size at which it is served. We characterize both
2420	below.
2421	Throughputacrossprefill-anddecode-heavyworkloads.Figure15comparesmax-throughput
2422	serving on GB200 NVL72 for two representative settings: a decode-heavy 8K input / 64K output
2423	workload and a prefill-heavy 50K input / 2K output workload, both at NVFP4 precision with
2424	speculative decoding disabled. Prefill is compute-bound, so per-token cost tracks FLOPs, which
2425	are set by the number of active parameters; Nemotron 3 Ultra pays roughly a3.2× FLOPs penalty
2426	against Qwen-3.5-397B-17B (55B versus 17B active parameters), so the MoE GEMMs are the
2427	dominant bottleneck and Nemotron 3 Ultra trails on the prefill-heavy workload. In large-batch
2428	decode, routing activates essentially all experts and per-step cost is instead set by total weight
2429	I/O, where the gap shrinks to roughly1.39× (550B versus 397B total parameters). With the MoE
2430	penalty that much smaller, the token-mixing mechanism becomes the deciding factor, and Nemotron
2431	3 Ultra’s Mamba-2 state-space layers, whose per-step decode cost is constant in sequence length, let
2432	it lead on the decode-heavy workload despite trailing on prefill.
2433	Speculative decoding for hybrid models.Multi-Token Prediction (see §2) reduces main-model
2434	forward passes at the cost of running the draft head and verifying candidates. The operating point
2435	depends on batch size: at small batches per-pass cost is dominated by weight reads, verification
2436	overhead is cheap, and high draft length wins for latency; at large batches per-pass cost is dominated
2437	by compute, verification overhead eats into throughput, and lower draft lengths, or disabling MTP,
2438	often win. We expose draft length as a deployment-time knob. Figure 16 sweeps draft length on a
2439	representative low-latency operating point: the NVFP4 checkpoint on a single-user workload with
2440	ISL/OSL/BS = 10K/16K/1, on a single GB200 node at TP=4.
2441	Hybrid Mamba models raise a second question: how to roll back state when a draft token is rejected.
2442	For pure Attention this is a per-token KV truncation; the Mamba SSM state, however, is a single
2443	fixed-size entry per sequence that is overwritten every token, so no state corresponding to an earlier
2444	token is directly available. We address this by snapshotting the SSM state at every draft step. The
2445	same snapshotting mechanism, run at a coarser cadence (every fixed number of tokens), also gives us
2446	prefix caching across requests, otherwise unavailable for Mamba, since prefix reuse in pure Attention
2447	is a free consequence of the per-token KV cache.

2487	Parallelism choices and wide expert parallelism.Nemotron 3 Ultra is too large to fit on a
2488	single GPU and must be parallelized across multiple ranks. The relevant axes are tensor parallelism
2489	(TP, which shards the weight matrices of each linear layer across ranks), expert parallelism (EP,
2490	which distributes full routed experts across ranks while Attention and Mamba remain data-parallel),
2491	and combinations of the two, TP within a group of ranks for Attention and Mamba, with routed
2492	experts EP-sharded across and within those groups. At small batch sizes inference is bound by
2493	weight-read memory bandwidth, and wider TP wins: spreading weights across more ranks reduces
2494	per-step HBM traffic by the TP factor, while the NVLink AllReduce of a single hidden-state vector
2495	is negligible by comparison. At large batch sizes communication of activation tensors becomes the
2496	bottleneck, and EP wins: inter-rank traffic is confined to the all-to-all dispatch and combine that
2497	bracket each routed-expert block, with no AllReduce on the critical path of any GEMM, Attention,
2498	Mamba, and the routed experts all run rank-local under EP. For Nemotron 3 Ultra, this makes wide
2499	EP the practical choice for high-throughput serving and wide TP the practical choice for low-latency
2500	serving; in some low-latency settings we have also observed that combining TP and EP, along with
2501	DP for Attention and Mamba, outperforms either alone. Wide-EP serving in particular requires
2502	careful load balancing across data-parallel ranks: because the routed-expert all-to-all is synchronous,
2503	an under-loaded rank stalls the entire group, so we route incoming requests to the least-loaded worker
2504	to keep per-rank token counts close. Expert-level imbalance within each MoE layer can be similarly
2505	addressed by replicating hot experts across EP ranks (EPLB). GB200 NVL72 is well-matched to all
2506	of these configurations, most significantly for high-throughput: all 72 GPUs share a single NVLink
2507	domain, so wide EP can span the full system without paying for cross-domain interconnects in the
2508	all-to-all path. Wide TP benefits from the same property for latency-bound serving, though only
2509	up to the point at which per-rank weight reads shrink enough that AllReduce becomes the new
2510	bottleneck.

2520	very differently, as the workload comparison above shows; serving both phases on a single replica
2521	therefore forces a single parallelism configuration and scheduling policy across two workloads with
2522	very different requirements. Prefill-decode disaggregation, which runs the two phases on separate
2523	workers with their own parallelism and scheduling, is the established response, and we adopt it for
2524	Nemotron 3 Ultra. Disaggregation requires transferring the KV cache from prefill to decode workers
2525	on every request; for hybrid Mamba-Attention models extra care is needed to ensure both the KV
2526	cache and the Mamba SSM state are transferred correctly, and that consumers of cache-state events
2527	can tell the two apart. We landed the necessary upstream changes, including the semantic KV-event
2528	metadata path that identifies hybrid cache groups and the NIXL side-channel host-resolution fix
2529	needed for multi-node Ray, and disaggregation for hybrid Mamba-Attention models now works
2530	out-of-the-box in vLLM (Kwon et al., 2023). End-to-end we currently measure up to roughly 10%
2531	throughput improvement from disaggregation on Nemotron 3 Ultra on prefill-heavy workloads, and
2532	expect further gains as the software stack matures.
2533	All-to-all backend.Under expert parallelism, the routed-expert all-to-all is the dominant inter-
2534	rank communication during MoE serving. It accounts for roughly 15% to 20% of total runtime on
2535	prefill-heavy workloads (50K input / 2K output tokens). The default vLLM scheme implements
2536	this all-to-all as an AllGather of activations followed by a ReduceScatter of expert outputs, simple,
2537	dependency-free, and topology-agnostic, but intrinsically wasteful: AllGather replicates every token
2538	on every rank, when each rank only needs the subset routed to its experts. We evaluated several true
2539	all-to-all backends and adopted FlashInfer’s NVLinkOneSided implementation (NVIDIA TensorRT
2540	LLM Team, 2026b) as the best end-to-end choice for Nemotron 3 Ultra serving on GB200 NVL72.
2541	End-to-end we measure roughly 5% throughput improvement from this backend over the default
2542	vLLM scheme; performance analysis indicates the all-to-all kernel itself still has room for further
2543	optimization. A more fundamental alternative is to avoid the all-to-all altogether: DWDP (NVIDIA
2544	TensorRT LLM Team, 2026a) keeps execution data-parallel and instead pulls each layer’s expert
2545	weights to every rank, prefetched behind the preceding compute so the transfer is hidden.
2546	Prefill and MoE chunking.On prefill-heavy workloads (e.g. 50K input / 2K output), the natural
2547	scheduling choice is to chunk prefill at the request level so chunks can be interleaved with decode
2548	forward passes. Small chunks at moderate-to-high batch sizes leave essentially no pure-decode passes,
2549	hurting user interactivity (TPOT), and at large batch sizes the number of prefill passes per request
2550	can exceed the number of decode passes. Growing the chunk size resolves this, but exposes a second
2551	50

2553	Nemotron 3 Ultra : Open, Efficient Mixture-of-Experts Hybrid Mamba-Transformer Model for Agentic Reasoning
2554	issue under wide expert parallelism: while Attention and Mamba are DP-sharded and each rank
2555	processes onlyconcurrency/DP requests, the routed-expert kernels process the union of tokens from
2556	all data-parallel ranks. Large prefill chunks therefore drive the routed-expert kernels into a regime
2557	where kernel-level resource limits become binding. The fix is MoE-side chunking, splitting the token
2558	batch within the MoE kernel itself, so chunk size can grow without hitting these limits. We landed
2559	this fix upstream in vLLM.
2560	GEMM dimensions and weight padding.Several combinations of tensor parallelism factor,
2561	quantization format, and target hardware land the per-rank GEMM dimensions at sizes that violate
2562	kernel alignment requirements. In every such case the route we have taken is to pad the affected
2563	weight matrices at load time so the kernel sees an acceptable shape, with runtime infrastructure
2564	adjusted to ignore the padded positions. Examples include MoE NVFP4 kernels whose hidden- or
2565	intermediate-dimension alignment requirements exceed what naturally falls out of the architecture,
2566	and Marlin NVFP4 linear and MoE kernels on Hopper that impose tile- and thread-level alignment
2567	constraints on their inputs. A natural improvement for future model generations is to choose
2568	the model’s inner dimensions such that all expected (TP, quantization, hardware) tuples produce
2569	kernel-friendly shapes without requiring load-time padding.

2571	We present our most capable model yet – Nemotron 3 Ultra with 550 billion total and 55 billion
2572	active parameters. Nemotron 3 Ultra uses a MoE Hybrid Mamba-Attention architecture along with
2573	LatentMoE and MTP for optimal inference and accuracy. Nemotron 3 Ultra was pre-trained on
2574	20 trillion text tokens and then post-trained using SFT, RL, and MOPD. We show that our model
2575	attains 5x higher inference throughput than other state-of-the-art open LLMs while achieving on-par
2576	accuracy. We open-source the pre-trained, post-trained, and quantized checkpoints along with the
2577	training data for Nemotron 3 Ultra on HuggingFace.

3110	research capability in Professional Work - specifically across Finance MBA, Consulting MBA,
3111	Scientific Research in Chemistry PhD and Physics PhD. ProfBench tasks are based on real-
3112	world workflows and judged with rubric criteria annotated by professionals working in these
3113	domains. Specifically, we run evaluations with a search tool and browse tool enabled in order
3114	for the model to identify relevant context from the internet. We run all evaluations at 256K
3115	context length without any context management, and report scores averaged over 16 times.
3116	• Browsecomp. We evaluate BrowseComp with a custom agentic search harness using Tavily as
3117	the search and browsing provider, together with terminal access. To avoid loading all retrieved
3118	web content into the model context, search and browse results are persisted to a per-task
3119	disk workspace; the model receives only metadata/snippets and can selectively inspect saved
3120	pages with shell commands such as grep, head, and sed. This allows the model to retrieve
3121	relevant evidence surgically, slows context growth, and preserves all previously collected search
3122	information across context resets.
3123	• Vals.ai Finance Agent Benchmark (FAB v1.1).We evaluate on the Vals.ai Finance
3124	Agent Benchmark (Bigeard et al., 2025), which tests agents on entry-level financial analyst
3125	tasks spanning nine different categories, from simple retrieval to financial modeling and market
3126	analysis. While the full benchmark reports on a private test set of 337 questions, we evaluate
3127	on 200 questions: the 50 publicly available validation samples augmented with 150 additional
3128	samples from the privately licensed validation set. Agents are provided four tools in the
3129	no-web-search condition: EDGAR search (via SEC API), an HTML page parser, a retrieval
3130	tool for querying previously extracted content, and asubmit tool for producing the final
3131	answer. In the web search condition, a fifth tool, Google web search via Tavily, is additionally
3132	available. Since the benchmark is grounded in SEC filings, most questions are expected to be
3133	answerable from EDGAR directly; web search serves as a supplementary signal. Accuracy is
3134	judged against expert-written ground-truth answers using an LLM-as-judge (GPT-5.2, mode
3135	of three evaluations). We closely follow the open-source evaluation harness.33

背景(我已从 NVIDIA-NeMo/RL 仓库的 ultra-v3 分支指南中得知):后训练 pipeline 为 SFT → Student RLVR(GRPO, 两阶段 49k→65k 上下文) → 多个专门化 teacher(General/Reasoning/RLHF/IFBench/SWE) → MOPD(Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation)。训练数据 blends 开源在 HF: nvidia/Nemotron-RL-Ultra-Training-Blends。模型是 550B-A55B 的 hybrid Mamba-Transformer MoE(LatentMoE + MTP),pretraining 用 NVFP4,上下文扩展到 1M。

步骤建议:
1. 用 `curl -L -o /tmp/nemotron_ultra.pdf "https://research.nvidia.com/labs/nemotron/files/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3-Ultra-Technical-Report.pdf"` 下载 PDF。
2. 检查环境是否有 `pdftotext`(poppler-utils);如果有,执行 `pdftotext -layout /tmp/nemotron_ultra.pdf /tmp/nemotron_ultra.txt`,然后分段 Read(用 Grep 定位关键词:post-training, SFT, RLVR, GRPO, MOPD, distillation, teacher, QAT, quantization, NVFP4, MTP, reward, GenRM, hyperparameter 等)。若无 pdftotext,用 `python3 -m venv /tmp/pdfenv2 && /tmp/pdfenv2/bin/pip install pypdf` 后写脚本提取。

215	2. Pretraining
216	In this section, we provide details on the pretraining of Nemotron 3 Ultra. Specifically, we detail the
217	architecture, NVFP4 pretraining recipe, data, and hyperparameters used for Nemotron 3 Ultra 550B-
218	A55B Base. We also share details on the long context extension phase, model training instabilities,
219	and benchmark accuracies.
220	2.1. Model Architecture
221	Nemotron 3 Ultra uses the same hybrid Mamba-Attention Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) architecture as
222	Nemotron 3 Super (NVIDIA, 2026), extended to 550B total parameters with 55B active parameters
223	per token. As with Nemotron 3 Super, we leverage LatentMoE (Elango et al., 2026) for MoE layers
224	and native Multi-Token Prediction for inference acceleration with two heads during pre-training.
225	Both MTP heads share the same parameters to enable robust autoregressive drafting as described
226	in NVIDIA (2026) and consist of a single attention layer followed by a single MoE layer. The layer
227	pattern and configuration for Nemotron 3 Ultra are shown in Figure 2 and Table 1, respectively.

436	2.3.6. Data Mixture and Ordering
437	The data mixtures used to train Nemotron 3 Ultra are an adaptation of the data mixtures used
438	to train Nemotron 3 Super and Nano (NVIDIA, 2025b, 2026), and incorporate new and refreshed
439	datasets. Following Feng et al. (2024), we design our data mixtures to balance diversity and quality.
440	We adopt the proposed two-phase curriculum and transition from a data mixture which biases
441	dataset diversity (phase 1) to a data mixture which biases dataset quality (phase 2). This transition
442	occurs after∼15trillion tokens corresponding to∼75%of pretraining. We present the high-level
443	breakdown for the phase 1 and phase 2 data mixtures in Figure 4. More detail on quality estimation
444	and dataset composition are available in Feng et al. (2024) and the Nemotron 3 Super and Nano
445	reports (NVIDIA, 2025b, 2026).
446	The pretraining corpus spans 19 high level categories across both data mixtures. The largest
447	component, accounting for∼49%of phase 1 tokens and ∼38%of phase 2 tokens, consists of
448	quality-filtered and synthetic web crawl data: crawl-medium, crawl-medium-high, crawl-high, syn-
449	crawl-medium, and syn-crawl-high. Other categories include finepdfs (Kydlíček et al., 2025) which
450	we quality-filter and upweight for inclusion in phase 2, math data (Mahabadi et al., 2025; Akter et al.,
451	2025), code data, Nemotron-CC-Code, Wikipedia, academic texts, legal data, multilingual data
452	spanning 11 languages (Arabic, Chinese, French, German, Hebrew, Hindi, Italian, Japanese, Korean,
453	Portuguese, Spanish), Crawl++, and synthetic SFT-style data. Crawl++ consists of OpenWebText,
454	BigScience (Laurençon et al., 2023), and Reddit datasets. The SFT-style data, subcategorized
455	as sft-code, sft-stem, and sft-general, we include per Akter et al. (2026) who demonstrate its
456	effectiveness.

551	Besides the long-context document QA data we used in Nemotron 3 Super & Nano, we further added
552	long-context SFT-style data into the blend. We did not use any RULER-style data in the blend.
553	Overall, the long-context data was 46% and Phase 2 data was 54% in the blend. We performed
554	CPT on 1,048,576 (1M) context length for 92% of the iterations, while we trained on 4,096 (4K)
555	for the remaining 8% of the time in order to maintain the accuracy of the short benchmarks. Note
556	that each iteration was trained with either 1M or 4K length and we did not mix sequence lengths
557	within an iteration. Each iteration we constantly trained for 25,165,824 tokens. We only put math
558	and code SFT-style data into the 4K iterations, since we found it worked best to maintain the short
559	benchmark metrics while achieving strong long-context RULER scores. Eventually, the LC-Phase

847	3.1. Supervised Fine Tuning
848	To train the student model, we start from the pre-trained base model and perform Supervised
849	Fine-Tuning (SFT) in two stages, following Nemotron 3 Super (NVIDIA, 2026). In Stage 1, we train
850	on packed sequences of length294,912tokens with global batch size64for204 ,800samples, using a
851	cosine learning-rate schedule with peak learning rate1.5× 10−5, minimum learning rate1× 10−6,
852	and9 ,600warmup samples. In Stage 2, we extend packed sequence to515,000tokens, augmenting
853	the mixture with additional long-context data up to512K tokens. We train with global batch size64
854	for19 ,200samples, using the same learning-rate schedule with peak1× 10−5 to minimum2× 10−6
855	and6 ,400warmup samples. As in pre-training, we retain the shared-weight MTP objective during
856	SFT, using two MTP layers with a per-token auxiliary-loss scaling factor of0.1.
857	3.1.1. Data
858	Long Context.We prepare 512K long-context SFT data based on the synthetic data pipeline
859	following (NVIDIA, 2026). Our data is aimed at improving long-context abilities including, but not
860	limited to multi-document reasoning, sequential scanning, and querying synthetic tables.
861	15

863	Nemotron 3 Ultra : Open, Efficient Mixture-of-Experts Hybrid Mamba-Transformer Model for Agentic Reasoning
864	Efficiency and Control.The SFT data include two components for reasoning efficiency and
865	control. The first is training samples generated by GPT-OSS-120B in its medium-effort mode on
866	prompts of math reasoning, STEM question answering and instruction following. These SFT data
867	initiate Ultra’s medium-effort mode which is later optimized during the RLVR stage. The second
868	component is training samples where the reasoning traces are truncated to random reasoning budgets
869	while the responses remain the same. This is similar to Nemotron 3 Nano and Super with one design
870	change: the</think>tokens in the truncated samples are masked from SFT training loss.
871	Safety.To instill robust safety behaviors, first, we retain the45K safety data blend curated
872	in Nemotron 3 Super (NVIDIA, 2026) with prompts curated from diverse sources and responses
873	synthetically generated conditioned on a response policy mapped to each prompt. Our two-stage
874	response and reasoning generation framework enables deliberate reflection on safety guidelines in
875	the reasoning traces and ensures that the final responses are consistent, policy-compliant, and
876	contextually appropriate. Further, to curate a multilingual set for Nemotron 3 Ultra training,
877	we translated the Nemotron 3 Super safety data blend into six languages — German, Spanish,
878	French, Japanese, Italian, and Chinese - using NeMo Skills’ chunked translation capability, ensuring
879	sentence-by-sentence parity, and paired with NVIDIA Riva Translate 4B v1.1 as the translation
880	backbone.
881	To improve translation quality, each translated example was back-translated into English and
882	compared against the original English prompt-response pair. Examples with semantic similarity
883	below 0.8 were filtered out, removing approximately≈ 10− 15%of examples per translated language.
884	The highest- and lowest-scoring translations were manually spot-checked to verify that this filter
885	was removing examples with clear translation failures or structural issues. After filtering, we used
886	stratified sampling to create a balanced dataset across the six translated languages. The final safety
887	blend contains about≈ 135K samples:≈ 45K in English and≈ 15K from each of the translated
888	languages.
889	Search Capabilities.During SFT, we expose the model to search data spanning different difficulty
890	levels and tool-use harnesses to improve generalization.
891	First, we retain the search trajectories from the Nemotron 3 Super (NVIDIA, 2026) dataset,
892	whose seed prompts are grounded in the Wikidata knowledge graph. Specifically, the dataset
893	selects well-connected hub entities and performs 4–8 hop random walks over factual relations to
894	construct multi-hop search prompts. These prompts are then solved using Tavily Search Engine
895	(https://www.tavily.com/), with MiniMax 2.1 serving as the teacher model.

1048	3.1.2. Data Packing
1049	To train efficiently on a large and diverse collection of datasets, we adopt a length-aware best-fit
1050	packing strategy (Ding et al., 2024), which packs multiple conversations into sequences up to a
1051	maximum context length. Our packer is highly memory-efficient: it reads and interleaves all source
1052	files in a round-robin fashion, maintains only a fixed-size pool of open sequences in memory, and
1053	retires a sequence once its residual capacity falls below a small tolerance. Each incoming conversation
1054	is assigned to the partially filled sequence whose remaining capacity it most tightly fits, following a
1055	best-fit rule that minimizes padding overhead. We neither truncate nor split conversations, preserving
1056	complete context and reducing hallucinations. Additionally, we enforce an in-pack deduplication
1057	19

1059	Nemotron 3 Ultra : Open, Efficient Mixture-of-Experts Hybrid Mamba-Transformer Model for Agentic Reasoning
1060	constraint to prevent identical prompts from co-occurring within the same sequence. After packing,
1061	we perform a final shuffle over all completed packs. Overall, our implementation ensures that each
1062	packed sequence draws from a broad, well-mixed cross-section of the data distribution rather than
1063	clustering examples from any single source. This thorough mixing is essential at scale, where naive
1064	concatenation of per-source shards would otherwise induce strong distributional locality and degrade
1065	optimization stability.

1082	3.3. MOPD
1083	Mixed-environment RLVR provides broad capability improvements across a wide range of domains.
1084	However, as the number of environments continues to grow, each domain contributes only a relatively
1085	small number of samples to any given training batch, diluting the per-domain learning signal and
1086	making it increasingly difficult to balance training across domains. To fully unlock performance and
1087	push the frontier in each capability area, we train more than ten specialized teacher models, each
1088	optimized through its own domain-specific training pipeline.
1089	During MOPD, the student model (obtained from RLVR) generates rollouts across all domains
1090	and receives dense reward signals from the corresponding teacher models. To maximize efficiency,
1091	MOPD is conducted asynchronously, with student rollout generation, teacher scoring, and student
1092	optimization fully pipelined. Moreover, MOPD is performed over multiple iterative cycles: after
1093	obtaining an MOPD-trained checkpoint, we branch out new rounds of teacher training initialized from
1094	the updated student model and subsequently merge the resulting improvements back into the next
1095	MOPD stage. This iterative co-evolution between student and teachers enables continuous capability
1096	improvement and progressively stronger specialization across domains. On training Nemotron 3
1097	Ultra, we conduct two iterations of MOPD, with exact procedure shown in Figure 10.

1440	One key finding from our MOPD trials is that teacher models trained with substantially different
1441	training pipelines cannot be effectively combined through a straightforward MOPD merge, resulting in

1441	training pipelines cannot be effectively combined through a straightforward MOPD merge, resulting in
1442	suboptimal performance. We hypothesize that when the teacher and student are trained on different
1443	SFT data, they acquire different reasoning behaviors and induce different output distributions. This
1444	distribution mismatch can cause student-generated trajectories to be out-of-distribution for the
1445	teacher, reducing the quality and reliability of the supervision signals provided by the teacher. We
1446	encountered this issue in practice because the teacher and student models were developed in parallel,
1447	with many of the agentic and reasoning teachers trained using their own specialized SFT pipelines.
1448	To mitigate the distribution mismatch between teacher and student models, we introduce a brief
1449	warmup stage before MOPD. Specifically, the student undergoes a very light SFT on data drawn
1450	from the teacher’s training distribution. The objective is to align the student’s reasoning trajectories
1451	and output distribution with those expected by the teacher. This improves the reliability of teacher
1452	supervision by increasing the likelihood that student-generated trajectories remain within the
1453	teacher’s support. Since the warmup stage is intentionally limited in scale, it induces minimal
1454	regression on unrelated domains, and any residual degradation is subsequently recovered through
1455	MOPD training.

1512	3.3.5. Limitations and Open Problems
1513	In this section we will discuss several aspects of MOPD that remain unresolved and would benefit
1514	from further study. During the development of MOPD, we evaluated several technically plausible
1515	variants that did not improve performance under our current experimental setup. We share these
1516	observations to make the empirical picture more complete, but they should not be interpreted as
1517	evidence that these approaches are fundamentally ineffective. With further research, we believe
1518	these directions could yield MOPD approaches that outperform our current setup, and we encourage
1519	the community to continue exploring them.
1520	• Logit matching.A natural alternative to the sampled-token objective is distribution-level
1521	distillation, where the student is trained to match the teacher’s predictive distribution over
1522	the top-𝑘 tokens or the full vocabulary at each prefix. In our preliminary experiments, these
1523	objectives did not improve MOPD performance and consistently underperformed the sampled-
1524	token objective on some agentic benchmarks such as Terminal Bench. We hypothesize that
1525	full-distribution matching may impose an overly strong local constraint on prefixes sampled
1526	from the student policy, particularly when those prefixes have limited support under the teacher
1527	distribution. In this regime, teacher logits can become poorly calibrated or less informative,
1528	and matching the full distribution may amplify noise from off-support states. By contrast,
1529	the sampled-token objective applies supervision only to realized actions and may therefore
1530	28

1533	provide a more stable on-policy learning signal. Characterizing when broader distributional
1534	supervision is beneficial remains an open problem.
1535	• Foundations for MOPD.As discussed above, MOPD is most effective when student-
1536	generated trajectories remain within the teacher’s support, allowing the teacher to provide
1537	reliable supervision. One possible approach is to ensure that the teacher and student share a
1538	unified SFT stage before specialization. Another is to first develop specialized teachers, use
1539	them to generate SFT data, and then train the student with this data before applying RL
1540	or MOPD. Due to time and resource constraints, we did not systematically evaluate these
1541	alternatives in this project and will leave them for future work.
1542	• MOPD on long-horizon tasks.Agentic workflows require many turns of tool calls and
1543	environment interactions, whereas reasoning tasks are typically single-turn. When mixing end-

1549	end-to-end rollouts can yield further gains, and how to make it robust to potential distribution

1737	Ray GCS Scalability and Slurm Launch Overheads
1738	The NeMo-RL job is heterogeneous, it must launch different roles (training workers, vLLM generation
1739	workers, gym workers, and judge workers), each with different resource requirements, across different
1740	node subsets. At the start of post-training, our RL launch script issued multiple, separatesrun
1741	invocations per node to assign each node its role, start its processes, and monitor progress. Each
1742	srun is an RPC to the Slurm controller daemon (slurmctld), which must process them serially. At
1743	scale, this meant hundreds of serial RPCs queued againstslurmctld, a pattern that scaled𝑂(𝑛)
1744	with the node count and quickly became a scaling bottleneck. Restructuring to a single multi-node
1745	srun reduced Slurm controller interactions to𝑂(1). Together, startup cost dropped from over 30
1746	minutes to 10 minutes..
1747	Additionally, the RL job creates a massive number of Ray actors simultaneously across policy,
1748	generation, and environment workers. At 3K+ GPU scale, Ray’s single-threaded Global Control
1749	Service (GCS) was overwhelmed by actor registrations, causing long startups (25-49 minutes) and
1750	thundering-herd startup failures. We eliminated 40% of actor registrations by converting short-lived
1751	actors to tasks, pooling initialization actors per node, and applied aggressive GCS tuning. Anyscale
1752	resolved the GCS scalability regressions with the fixes shipped in the Ray 2.55 public release.
1753	Topology-Aware NVLink Domain Placement
1754	On GB200 NVL72, the NVLink domain spans an entire rack (72 GPUs across 18 nodes). Without
1755	topology awareness during worker placement, Megatron’s Expert Parallelism (EP) groups can span
1756	multiple racks, forcing MoE all-to-all communication over InfiniBand instead of NVLink.
1757	NeMo RL had no concept of NVLink domains: Ray node IDs are random UUIDs with no topological
1758	relation, and Megatron trusts the rank order it receives. If the framework assigns ranks without
1759	NVLink domain awareness, EP groups will silently span racks. The fix was to make rank assignment
1760	domain-aware and ensure all GPUs within an EP group are co-located on the same rack. Note that
1761	inter-rack ordering is not a concern here, as our DP size does not require exploiting cross-rack rail
1762	optimizations.
1763	The fix was threefold. First, at container startup (beforeray start ), ray.sub generates and sources
1764	a probe script that parses the NVLink fabricClusterUUID from nvidia-smi -q – a hex string
1765	identical for all GPUs in the same NVLink domain – and registers it as a Ray custom resource
1766	(nvlink_domain_<ClusterUUID>), giving the scheduler rack-membership information it previously
1767	lacked. The same probe derives a topology rank (topo_rank) from SLURM_TOPOLOGY_ADDR, falling
1768	back to SLURM_PROCID or hostname digits. Second, inside NeMo RL’sRayVirtualCluster, bundle
1769	indices are sorted by a( domain_min_topo_rank,topo_rank,gpu_id )composite key, ordering
1770	NVLink domains by their minimum topology rank and nodes within each domain by physical
1771	position, so that EP groups remain within a single NVLink domain. When segment_size is
1772	33

1775	set, bundles from domains that cannot contribute a complete segment are discarded. The sorted
1776	order drives per-worker RANK and CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES assignment, and Megatron runs with
1777	external_gpu_device_mapping=True so it trusts Ray’s GPU pinning rather than re-deriving device
1778	placement. Third, thetopo_rank (from SLURM_TOPOLOGY_ADDR) corrects the scrambled Slurm block
1779	ordering, with ray.sub additionally applying a deterministic hostname sort before Ray head-node
1780	assignment.
1781	With these changes, training and generation actors are co-located in the same NVLink domain, and
1782	EP all-to-all traffic stays on NVLink instead of falling back to InfiniBand.

1784	NUMA Binding for Policy and vLLM Workers
1785	On GB200 NVL72, each compute tray contains a Grace CPU with two sockets and multiple NUMA
1786	nodes. GPUs are physically affiliated with specific CPU sockets: GPUs 0 and 1 map to NUMA
1787	node 0, while GPUs 2 and 3 map to NUMA node 1. Without explicit NUMA binding, Ray worker
1788	processes, both Megatron policy workers and vLLM generation workers, could be scheduled on
1789	CPU cores belonging to the remote socket relative to their assigned GPUs. On Grace-Blackwell,
1790	the NVLink-C2C interconnect between Grace CPU and Blackwell GPU is socket-local, so cross-
1791	socket placement forces memory traffic to traverse the inter-socket coherence link before reaching
1792	NVLink-C2C, degrading GPU memory bandwidth.
1793	The fix was to explicitly bind policy and vLLM worker processes to the CPU socket local to their
1794	assigned GPUs. This ensures that optimizer state offloading (e.g., CPU↔GPU transfers during
1795	checkpointing and weight refit), tokenization, data preprocessing, and pinned-memory allocations all
1796	hit local DRAM and use the socket-local C2C path. This optimization delivered a10% end-to-end
1797	throughput improvementon GB200.
1798	Checkpoint Save Blocking
1799	Synchronous checkpoint saves blocked training for∼60s per save. Enabling asynchronous checkpoint-
1800	ing from the Nvidia Resiliency Extension (NVRx), where model parameters are copied to CPU and
1801	persisted in the background while training continues, reduced the exposed blocking time to∼6–8
1802	seconds. Two additional optimizations reduced this further: overlapped NCCL transfers with D2H
1803	copies to shrink the synchronous staging window, and persistent checkpoint worker processes that
1804	avoid fork/spawn overhead on each save. We further moved checkpoint finalization, the cross-worker
1805	synchronization and the final commit, onto a background thread so it never blocks training, and we
1806	cache the distributed save plan so it is computed once rather than on every save. With the Megatron
1807	Core Distributed Optimizer, which shards optimizer state across data-parallel ranks so each rank
1808	only saves its local slice, the exposed save time reduces to<1 second.

1841	Multi-Node vLLM Operational Stability
1842	Multi-node vLLM uses Ray as its distributed executor. Each vLLM data-parallel leader spawns
1843	EngineCore subprocesses that each callray.init() to connect to the Global Control Store (GCS).
1844	At scale, this creates additional GCS connections on top of the actor creation burst. Beyond the JIT
1845	cache contention addressed in the previous section, three additional issues caused startup failures at
1846	scale:
1847	• Package and kernel ABI mismatches.Independent components of the RL stack (policy
1848	training, generation, environment services) installed different versions of shared GPU kernel
1849	libraries. ABI differences between versions meant precompiled kernels from one component
1850	could not be reused by another, causing silent crashes at initialization.
1851	• Subprocess environment divergence.Environment variables set in the main Ray actor
1852	process were not propagated to subprocesses spawned viamultiprocessing.spawn, causing
1853	them to resolve different library versions than the parent and fail at kernel load time.
1854	• Collective-communication incompatibilities.Certain JIT-compiled kernels were incom-
1855	patible with NCCL’s multi-node NVLink memory registration on GB200, causing hangs during
1856	distributed initialization.
1857	These were addressed as follows:
1858	• Dependency unification.All components of the RL stack were aligned to a single version

1863	• Environment propagation.Library paths and environment variables were explicitly for-

1865	• Collective-communication workaround.Multi-node NVLink memory registration was
1866	disabled for the affected kernel paths until an upstream fix in FlashInfer was available.
1867	• vLLMHealth checks to validate device allocations and communications over the TP NCCL
1868	group, RPC timeouts to prevent infinite waits on stalled workers, and graceful shutdown along
1869	with orphan process cleanup were all implemented to improve operational stability across jobs.
1870	Container and Storage I/O
1871	At scale, every node simultaneously reads the container image (∼44 GB squashfs) from shared
1872	storage at job startup, producing tens of terabytes of concurrent reads across thousands of parallel
1873	I/O streams. This overwhelmed the storage subsystem: a subset of nodes either hitInput/output
1874	error or stalled for 12+ minutes during container extraction (vs.∼2 to 3 minutes under normal
1875	conditions). Because all workers must be ready before Ray initialization begins, a single slow node
1876	delays the entire job. Additionally, at job completion all nodes concurrently write back JIT caches
1877	to shared storage, creating a second I/O storm that degraded storage availability for other jobs on
1878	the cluster.
1879	These were addressed with two complementary strategies:
1880	• Container caching.Enroot’s local squashfs cache ensures that once a node has extracted
1881	the container image, subsequent jobs reuse the cached local copy, effectively eliminating the
1882	shared storage read load for warm nodes.
1883	• Asymmetric read/write cache paths.During training, all JIT writes go to node-local
1884	storage, producing zero shared storage writes. At job completion, a single designated sidecar
1885	process archives the caches back to shared storage as compressed tarballs, rather than all nodes
1886	writing simultaneously. Since all nodes compile identical kernels, only one node’s cache needs
1887	to be persisted. At startup, each node extracts these tarballs into local storage via a single
1888	sequential read per cache type, avoiding metadata-intensive small-file I/O entirely.

2257	4.5. SSM Cache Optimization
2258	In Mamba autoregressive decoding, the SSM state is stored in a constant-sized cache for each batch
2259	element. The KV cache size, on the other hand, grows with sequence length. However, there is a
2260	crossover point below which the Mamba cache size is larger than the KV cache size. For example, in
2261	Nemotron 3 Ultra, the 32-bit Mamba cache is larger than the FP8 KV cache at sequence lengths up
2262	to 64K. This is illustrated in Figure 14.
2263	Therefore, depending on the sequence length and batch size, the Mamba cache can become both a
2264	DRAM-footprint bottleneck and a source of DRAM-read pressure that limits decoding speed.
2265	To address this, we quantize the Mamba SSM cache from the original FP32 precision to lower
2266	precisions. Following Nemotron 3 Super (NVIDIA, 2026), we first adopt 16-bit cache precision,
2267	where FP16 with stochastic rounding preserves FP32-cache accuracy and verbosity.
2268	To further improve cache compression, we also explore 8-bit Mamba cache quantization formats. We
2269	evaluated this on Nemotron 3 Super.

2326	We release a single NVFP4 checkpoint for Nemotron 3 Ultra that targets both Blackwell, where
2327	it runs with native FP4 math, and Hopper, where it runs as W4A16 (weights NVFP4, activations
2328	BF16). This is because Hopper lacks native FP4 tensor cores. KV Cache is quantized to FP8 and
2329	Mamba cache data type is FP16 with stochastic rounding.
2330	The natural candidate for Hopper would have been a separate FP8 checkpoint to un-lock FP8
2331	tensor-core math. At first glance W8A8 should be the better Hopper choice: FP8 tensor cores have
2332	higher peak throughput than the BF16 math the W4A16 path relies on. In practice the opposite
2333	holds at Nemotron 3 Ultra’s scale. With TP=8 on an 8-GPU H100 node (640GiB of aggregate
2334	HBM), the FP8 checkpoint (≈ 540GiB) leaves roughly10GiB per GPU for activations, KV cache,
2335	and Mamba state, against roughly40GiB for the NVFP4 checkpoint (≈ 330GiB). The tight FP8
2336	cache budget caps the maximum batch size at the operating points we care about, which keeps the
2337	workload memory-bandwidth-bound and prevents us from ever reaching the compute-bound regime
2338	where FP8 tensor cores would matter. The measured throughput-versus-user-latency Pareto places
2339	W4A16 on or above W8A8 across the relevant range.
2340	The case for the single NVFP4 checkpoint becomes much stronger once MTP is in the picture.
2341	The reduced W4 footprint leaves enough headroom to fit MTP weights on the same 8-GPU node,
2342	while the FP8 checkpoint cannot fit MTP without scaling to two H100 nodes and surrendering the
2343	single-NVLink-domain property. With MTP enabled on the W4A16 path, the throughput-versus-
2344	user-latency Pareto both moves up across the relevant range and extends much further into the
2345	low-latency regime than W8A8 reaches at any operating point.

2406	5. Inference
2407	Nemotron 3 Ultra inherits the inference-aware architecture of Nemotron 3 Super (NVIDIA, 2026):
2408	LatentMoE (Elango et al., 2026), which buys more routed experts at fixed inference cost by trading
2409	away hidden-dimension width; a hybrid Mamba-2 stack with sparse global Attention anchors,
2410	which gives sub-quadratic sequence-length scaling during prefill and a bounded KV-cache footprint
2411	during decode; and Multi-Token Prediction for native speculative decoding (see §2). Below we first
2412	characterize how these choices play out in practice across serving regimes — prefill- versus decode-
2413	heavy workloads and small- versus large-batch operation — and then turn to the considerations that
2414	come into focus when serving a model of this size, considerations that did not bind at Nemotron
2415	3 Super or Nemotron 3 Nano scale. Quantization recipes and the SSM-state cache treatment are
2416	covered in §4; headline throughput comparisons appear in §1.
2417	5.1. Performance across serving regimes
2418	Nemotron 3 Ultra’s effective inference performance depends strongly on the operating point: the
2419	prefill/decode balance of the workload and the batch size at which it is served. We characterize both
2420	below.
2421	Throughputacrossprefill-anddecode-heavyworkloads.Figure15comparesmax-throughput
2422	serving on GB200 NVL72 for two representative settings: a decode-heavy 8K input / 64K output
2423	workload and a prefill-heavy 50K input / 2K output workload, both at NVFP4 precision with
2424	speculative decoding disabled. Prefill is compute-bound, so per-token cost tracks FLOPs, which
2425	are set by the number of active parameters; Nemotron 3 Ultra pays roughly a3.2× FLOPs penalty
2426	against Qwen-3.5-397B-17B (55B versus 17B active parameters), so the MoE GEMMs are the
2427	dominant bottleneck and Nemotron 3 Ultra trails on the prefill-heavy workload. In large-batch
2428	decode, routing activates essentially all experts and per-step cost is instead set by total weight
2429	I/O, where the gap shrinks to roughly1.39× (550B versus 397B total parameters). With the MoE
2430	penalty that much smaller, the token-mixing mechanism becomes the deciding factor, and Nemotron
2431	3 Ultra’s Mamba-2 state-space layers, whose per-step decode cost is constant in sequence length, let
2432	it lead on the decode-heavy workload despite trailing on prefill.
2433	Speculative decoding for hybrid models.Multi-Token Prediction (see §2) reduces main-model
2434	forward passes at the cost of running the draft head and verifying candidates. The operating point
2435	depends on batch size: at small batches per-pass cost is dominated by weight reads, verification
2436	overhead is cheap, and high draft length wins for latency; at large batches per-pass cost is dominated
2437	by compute, verification overhead eats into throughput, and lower draft lengths, or disabling MTP,
2438	often win. We expose draft length as a deployment-time knob. Figure 16 sweeps draft length on a
2439	representative low-latency operating point: the NVFP4 checkpoint on a single-user workload with
2440	ISL/OSL/BS = 10K/16K/1, on a single GB200 node at TP=4.
2441	Hybrid Mamba models raise a second question: how to roll back state when a draft token is rejected.
2442	For pure Attention this is a per-token KV truncation; the Mamba SSM state, however, is a single
2443	fixed-size entry per sequence that is overwritten every token, so no state corresponding to an earlier
2444	token is directly available. We address this by snapshotting the SSM state at every draft step. The
2445	same snapshotting mechanism, run at a coarser cadence (every fixed number of tokens), also gives us
2446	prefix caching across requests, otherwise unavailable for Mamba, since prefix reuse in pure Attention
2447	is a free consequence of the per-token KV cache.

2486	5.2. Inference at Ultra Scale
2487	Parallelism choices and wide expert parallelism.Nemotron 3 Ultra is too large to fit on a
2488	single GPU and must be parallelized across multiple ranks. The relevant axes are tensor parallelism
2489	(TP, which shards the weight matrices of each linear layer across ranks), expert parallelism (EP,
2490	which distributes full routed experts across ranks while Attention and Mamba remain data-parallel),
2491	and combinations of the two, TP within a group of ranks for Attention and Mamba, with routed
2492	experts EP-sharded across and within those groups. At small batch sizes inference is bound by
2493	weight-read memory bandwidth, and wider TP wins: spreading weights across more ranks reduces
2494	per-step HBM traffic by the TP factor, while the NVLink AllReduce of a single hidden-state vector
2495	is negligible by comparison. At large batch sizes communication of activation tensors becomes the
2496	bottleneck, and EP wins: inter-rank traffic is confined to the all-to-all dispatch and combine that
2497	bracket each routed-expert block, with no AllReduce on the critical path of any GEMM, Attention,
2498	Mamba, and the routed experts all run rank-local under EP. For Nemotron 3 Ultra, this makes wide
2499	EP the practical choice for high-throughput serving and wide TP the practical choice for low-latency
2500	serving; in some low-latency settings we have also observed that combining TP and EP, along with
2501	DP for Attention and Mamba, outperforms either alone. Wide-EP serving in particular requires
2502	careful load balancing across data-parallel ranks: because the routed-expert all-to-all is synchronous,
2503	an under-loaded rank stalls the entire group, so we route incoming requests to the least-loaded worker
2504	to keep per-rank token counts close. Expert-level imbalance within each MoE layer can be similarly
2505	addressed by replicating hot experts across EP ranks (EPLB). GB200 NVL72 is well-matched to all
2506	of these configurations, most significantly for high-throughput: all 72 GPUs share a single NVLink
2507	domain, so wide EP can span the full system without paying for cross-domain interconnects in the
2508	all-to-all path. Wide TP benefits from the same property for latency-bound serving, though only
2509	up to the point at which per-rank weight reads shrink enough that AllReduce becomes the new
2510	bottleneck.
