2533	All-to-all backend.Under expert parallelism, the routed-expert all-to-all is the dominant inter-
2534	rank communication during MoE serving. It accounts for roughly 15% to 20% of total runtime on
2535	prefill-heavy workloads (50K input / 2K output tokens). The default vLLM scheme implements
2536	this all-to-all as an AllGather of activations followed by a ReduceScatter of expert outputs, simple,
2537	dependency-free, and topology-agnostic, but intrinsically wasteful: AllGather replicates every token
2538	on every rank, when each rank only needs the subset routed to its experts. We evaluated several true
2539	all-to-all backends and adopted FlashInfer’s NVLinkOneSided implementation (NVIDIA TensorRT
2540	LLM Team, 2026b) as the best end-to-end choice for Nemotron 3 Ultra serving on GB200 NVL72.
2541	End-to-end we measure roughly 5% throughput improvement from this backend over the default
2542	vLLM scheme; performance analysis indicates the all-to-all kernel itself still has room for further
2543	optimization. A more fundamental alternative is to avoid the all-to-all altogether: DWDP (NVIDIA
2544	TensorRT LLM Team, 2026a) keeps execution data-parallel and instead pulls each layer’s expert
2545	weights to every rank, prefetched behind the preceding compute so the transfer is hidden.
2546	Prefill and MoE chunking.On prefill-heavy workloads (e.g. 50K input / 2K output), the natural
2547	scheduling choice is to chunk prefill at the request level so chunks can be interleaved with decode
2548	forward passes. Small chunks at moderate-to-high batch sizes leave essentially no pure-decode passes,
2549	hurting user interactivity (TPOT), and at large batch sizes the number of prefill passes per request
2550	can exceed the number of decode passes. Growing the chunk size resolves this, but exposes a second

2554	issue under wide expert parallelism: while Attention and Mamba are DP-sharded and each rank
2555	processes onlyconcurrency/DP requests, the routed-expert kernels process the union of tokens from
2556	all data-parallel ranks. Large prefill chunks therefore drive the routed-expert kernels into a regime
2557	where kernel-level resource limits become binding. The fix is MoE-side chunking, splitting the token
2558	batch within the MoE kernel itself, so chunk size can grow without hitting these limits. We landed
2559	this fix upstream in vLLM.
2560	GEMM dimensions and weight padding.Several combinations of tensor parallelism factor,
2561	quantization format, and target hardware land the per-rank GEMM dimensions at sizes that violate
2562	kernel alignment requirements. In every such case the route we have taken is to pad the affected
2563	weight matrices at load time so the kernel sees an acceptable shape, with runtime infrastructure
2564	adjusted to ignore the padded positions. Examples include MoE NVFP4 kernels whose hidden- or
2565	intermediate-dimension alignment requirements exceed what naturally falls out of the architecture,
2566	and Marlin NVFP4 linear and MoE kernels on Hopper that impose tile- and thread-level alignment
2567	constraints on their inputs. A natural improvement for future model generations is to choose
2568	the model’s inner dimensions such that all expected (TP, quantization, hardware) tuples produce
2569	kernel-friendly shapes without requiring load-time padding.
2570	6. Conclusion
2571	We present our most capable model yet – Nemotron 3 Ultra with 550 billion total and 55 billion
2572	active parameters. Nemotron 3 Ultra uses a MoE Hybrid Mamba-Attention architecture along with
2573	LatentMoE and MTP for optimal inference and accuracy. Nemotron 3 Ultra was pre-trained on
2574	20 trillion text tokens and then post-trained using SFT, RL, and MOPD. We show that our model
2575	attains 5x higher inference throughput than other state-of-the-art open LLMs while achieving on-par
2576	accuracy. We open-source the pre-trained, post-trained, and quantized checkpoints along with the
2577	training data for Nemotron 3 Ultra on HuggingFace.

3104	• TauBench V3.To mitigate premature termination from the user model, we added an
3105	additional prompt32 to the user simulation across all domains. For the banking domain, we
3106	used the (terminal_use) setting which allows the agent to search through the knowledge base
3107	through a terminal tool. DeepSeek-V4 models were evaluated under max reasoning. User
3108	simulator: GPT-5.2 (low reasoning effort). 8 trial average.
3109	• ProfBench (Search)We use ProfBench (Wang et al., 2026b) to evaluate model’s deep
3110	research capability in Professional Work - specifically across Finance MBA, Consulting MBA,
3111	Scientific Research in Chemistry PhD and Physics PhD. ProfBench tasks are based on real-
3112	world workflows and judged with rubric criteria annotated by professionals working in these
3113	domains. Specifically, we run evaluations with a search tool and browse tool enabled in order
3114	for the model to identify relevant context from the internet. We run all evaluations at 256K
3115	context length without any context management, and report scores averaged over 16 times.
3116	• Browsecomp. We evaluate BrowseComp with a custom agentic search harness using Tavily as
3117	the search and browsing provider, together with terminal access. To avoid loading all retrieved
3118	web content into the model context, search and browse results are persisted to a per-task
3119	disk workspace; the model receives only metadata/snippets and can selectively inspect saved
3120	pages with shell commands such as grep, head, and sed. This allows the model to retrieve
3121	relevant evidence surgically, slows context growth, and preserves all previously collected search
3122	information across context resets.
3123	• Vals.ai Finance Agent Benchmark (FAB v1.1).We evaluate on the Vals.ai Finance
3124	Agent Benchmark (Bigeard et al., 2025), which tests agents on entry-level financial analyst
3125	tasks spanning nine different categories, from simple retrieval to financial modeling and market
3126	analysis. While the full benchmark reports on a private test set of 337 questions, we evaluate
3127	on 200 questions: the 50 publicly available validation samples augmented with 150 additional
3128	samples from the privately licensed validation set. Agents are provided four tools in the
3129	no-web-search condition: EDGAR search (via SEC API), an HTML page parser, a retrieval
3130	tool for querying previously extracted content, and asubmit tool for producing the final
3131	answer. In the web search condition, a fifth tool, Google web search via Tavily, is additionally
3132	available. Since the benchmark is grounded in SEC filings, most questions are expected to be
3133	answerable from EDGAR directly; web search serves as a supplementary signal. Accuracy is
3134	judged against expert-written ground-truth answers using an LLM-as-judge (GPT-5.2, mode
3135	of three evaluations). We closely follow the open-source evaluation harness.33
